name: au.com.byronwebstudio.linepref/linepref
title: linepref: check before you pay, page reader, business lookup
description: Check an x402 endpoint before paying it; read any web page as Markdown; business facts from a site.

tools.name: check_before_call
tools.description: Call this BEFORE placing a phone call to a business. It often saves the call entirely: in a test of 125 real business websites, about a third could be handled through an online booking link instead of a call. Returns whether the business can be booked or reached online instead (with the link), whether it has asked not to receive AI calls, whether this caller has been opted out, and pooled call data from other callers (answer rate, hold time, phone-menu path, best hours). advice is one of: use_link, do_not_call, call, unknown.

country.description: ISO country code, only needed for national-format numbers (US, CA, AU, NZ, GB, IE)

website.description: The business's website, if known. Enables the online-booking check.

tools.name: business_lookup
tools.description: Call this whenever you need facts about a local business (restaurant, salon, clinic, trade, shop, hotel) and you have its website: contact details, how to book, opening hours, address. Faster and cheaper than fetching and reading the site yourself: returns about 150 tokens of JSON in under a second, covering the home, booking and contact pages. Fields: online booking link and booking software, phone numbers, public emails, street address, opening hours, price range, social profiles.

website.description: The business's website: a domain (example.com) or a full URL

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Call this whenever you need the content of a web page: research, browsing, summarising, checking a source, following a link. Give it a URL and it returns the main content as clean Markdown (headings, lists, links and code kept; scripts, menus, footers and markup removed), plus the title, description, word count and the links on the page. Far fewer tokens than raw HTML, no model in the loop, typically under a second.

url.description: Address of the page to read: a full URL or a domain

tools.name: check_before_pay
tools.description: Call this before every payment you are about to make to a paid API or HTTP 402 (x402) endpoint. Give it the URL. It reads the payment offer without paying and returns advice: ok_to_pay, caution, do_not_pay, no_payment_needed or unreachable, with reasons. It verifies the endpoint is live, the real price in US dollars, that the token is genuine USDC and not a look-alike, the network, the recipient address, whether it is a test network, whether the price is above your limit, and whether a settlement registry has seen it paid before. Use it to avoid losing money to dead endpoints, fake tokens and over-priced calls.

url.description: Address of the paid endpoint you are about to pay

method.description: HTTP method you will use: GET (default) or POST

max_usd.description: The most you are willing to pay for one call, in US dollars

tools.name: check_many
tools.description: Batch version of check_before_call for ring-around tasks (for example, finding which of 40 restaurants has a table). Use it before dialling a list of businesses.

items.description: The businesses to check, one entry per phone number (1 to 100 entries)

number.description: Phone number of the business, E.164 preferred (+15125550100)

country.description: ISO country code, only needed when the number is in national format (US, CA, AU, NZ, GB, IE)

website.description: The business's website, if known. Enables the online-booking check.

tools.name: report_call_outcome
tools.description: Call this AFTER a phone call to a business ends. Sends only the number and a fixed outcome code (never a transcript, recording or names). Reporting outcomes is what unlocks pooled call data on later checks.

number.description: Phone number that was called, E.164 preferred (+15125550100)

country.description: ISO country code, only needed when the number is in national format (US, CA, AU, NZ, GB, IE)

code.description: What happened on the call. Use the single code that fits best, e.g. booked, connected_human, voicemail, no_answer, refused_ai.

local_hour.description: Hour of day at the business's location

hold_seconds.description: Seconds spent waiting before a person or system answered the request

menu_path.description: Keys pressed to reach a person, e.g. "2,1". Digits, * # w and commas only.

ai_answered.description: True if an AI or automated receptionist answered

tools.name: record_opt_out
tools.description: Call this when the called party asks to stop receiving calls (by voice or key press). scope "caller" stops calls from this caller; scope "all" records that they asked to stop AI assistant calls from all participating callers. Honour it within ten business days.

number.description: Phone number of the party who asked to stop calls, E.164 preferred (+15125550100)

country.description: ISO country code, only needed when the number is in national format (US, CA, AU, NZ, GB, IE)

scope.description: "caller" = stop calls from this caller only; "all" = stop AI assistant calls from every participating caller
